newsitem.title: USA: Payless Shoe gets favorable IRS ruling.
newsitem.headline: Payless Shoe gets favorable IRS ruling.

text.p: Payless ShoeSource Inc said Thursday it has received a favorable tax ruling from the Internal Revenue Service, which will allow the company to buy back $150 million worth of its outstanding common stock.
At the April 16, 1997 closing price of $41, the planned repurchase represents 3.7 million shares, or nine percent of the company's 39.9 million common shares outstanding.
The purchased shares will be held in the treasury for general corporate purposes.

In January 1997 the company's directors authorized the repurchase program. Before proceeding, the company sought a favorable ruling from the IRS to ensure that the program complies with tax rules applicable to companies that have been spun off in tax-free distributions. Payless was spun off from May Department Stores Co in May 1996.
Repurchases are expected to be made from time to time in the open market before the program expires on April 17, 1998. The repurchases may be discontinued at any time.
Payless ShoeSource operates 4,236 Payless footwear stores and 186 Parade of Shoes stores.
